title: Java Wrapper Classes
learningObjectives: Identify wrapper types for Java primitives.
Use boxing and unboxing between primitives and wrappers.
Convert numeric text with wrapper parsing methods.
Use wrapper constants and comparison methods safely.
Understand null risks when unboxing wrapper references.

understand.concept: Each Java primitive type has a corresponding wrapper class, such as int and Integer, double and Double, or boolean and Boolean. Wrappers are objects, so they can be used in generics and collections. Java supports autoboxing and unboxing, converting between primitives and wrappers automatically. Wrapper classes also provide parsing methods and constants. A wrapper reference may be null, and unboxing null throws NullPointerException.
understand.whyItMatters: This topic helps Java developers select and use the right standard-library tools for java wrapper classes in maintainable applications.
understand.analogy: Think of the collection or date API as a purpose-built tool: its operations communicate the guarantees your program can rely on.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is only a guide; Java API contracts, equality rules and exception behaviour determine the actual result.

explain.narrative: Use Integer.valueOf or Integer.parseInt to convert text to numeric values; parse methods return primitives while valueOf returns a wrapper. Autoboxing makes assignments such as Integer count = 5 possible. Unboxing converts the object back to a primitive. Prefer primitive types for ordinary numeric calculations when object behaviour is unnecessary. Compare wrapper values by value with equals or compare methods, not == when object identity could differ.

examples.title: Autoboxing and unboxing
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) { Integer boxed = 25; int value = boxed; System.out.println(value + 5); } }
examples.explanation: Assignment boxes an int and later unboxes the Integer.

examples.title: Parse an integer
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) { int count = Integer.parseInt("240"); System.out.println(count / 10); } }
examples.explanation: parseInt converts numeric text to a primitive int.

examples.title: Create a wrapper value
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) { Integer score = Integer.valueOf("87"); System.out.println(score); } }

examples.title: Use wrapper constants
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) { System.out.println(Integer.MAX_VALUE); System.out.println(Boolean.TRUE); } }
examples.explanation: Wrapper classes expose useful constants for their types.

examples.title: Compare by value
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) { Integer a = Integer.valueOf(500); Integer b = Integer.valueOf(500); System.out.println(a.equals(b)); System.out.println(Integer.compare(a, b)); } }
examples.explanation: equals compares wrapped values and compare returns zero for equal numbers.
